title: Investigation of the efficacy of a short-intervention implementing chairwork in patients with depressive disorders - a randomized controlled trial.
summary:
The present study investigates an emotion-focused, experience-oriented intervention, named chairwork from a cognitive-behavioral stance. It is conducted as a short-term psychotherapeutic treatment (3 sessions) for patients with depressive symptoms and aims to reduce self-criticism and increase self-compassion. In addition, the study aims at reducing depressive symptoms and increase self-esteem. 
During the intervention, different parts of the self are represented by chairs and thus become emotionally available and distinguishable for the patients. The position of the chairs in relation to each other and dialogues with and between the different parts are used. For example, the situation of a depressed patient who has difficulties getting out of bed in the morning could be represented by various chairs: One chair could symbolize the patient's inner critic (e.g. "you are a complete failure"), while another chair could represent the patient's emotions (sadness, despair). In a next step, a dialogical interaction is being initiated by the therapist, and functional coping mechanisms are being developed. Additionally, the patient is encouraged to take a step back and reflect onto the experienced inner mechanisms by looking at the scenario from a compassionate outside perspective. From this point of view, adaptive solutions shall be explored.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Depressive episode currently mild, moderate, or severe without psychotic symptoms.
Recurrent depressive episode, currently mild, moderate, or severe without psychotic symptoms. 
Fluent in spoken and written German.
Exclusion criteria:
Current psychotherapeutic treatment; acute suicidality; acute endangerment to others; acute self-harm; addictive disorders (current addictive disorder or harmful use); regular use of benzodiazepines; bipolar disorder (current or past episodes); acute psychotic symptoms; schizophrenic disorders (current or past); psychopharmacology: Stable intake of 4 weeks after reaching target dosage.
